problem: Large-model VLN methods convert visual observations to text, losing fine-grained visual information, and force the VLM to implicitly infer visual-topological relationships. They also usually act in a local action space and cannot backtrack.
motivation: VLMs are pretrained on static, disembodied vision-language tasks and have weak visual-spatial reasoning, which clashes with the embodied, spatially structured nature of navigation. Topological maps give traditional VLN methods explicit visual-spatial grounding and a global action space with backtracking. The paper asks whether injecting this structure architecturally into a small open-source VLM beats scaling up or prompting large proprietary models.
key_idea: Inject the online topological graph directly into a VLM by interleaving node images with node text and adding a learnable distance-based bias to self-attention (STAR-Att), so the model can choose over a global action space.
insight: Explicit architectural topology injection works better than describing the map in text. In the ablation, replacing text-based map prompts with STAR-Att gives SR 42.06 vs 40.70, with the no-map baseline at 39.76. Interleaving is critical: adding INP to the STAR-Att baseline raises SR from 26.14 to 38.40. Global actions add roughly 4-6 SR points. A fine-tuned 0.5B model with these priors nearly matches zero-shot GPT-4V-based MapGPT, and the 7B model surpasses it.
method: Online topological map: builds a graph of historical, candidate and current nodes. Historical and current nodes use 36-view panoramas. Candidate nodes use the view(s) that observed them, concatenated when seen from several positions. Edges are pairwise node distances.

Interleaved Navigation Prompt (INP): a frozen SigLIP ViT (798 tokens per node) plus an MLP projector encode each node. The visual tokens replace <image> placeholders inside the text right next to their node ID and type, and a structured system prompt is prepended.

STAR-Att: builds a token-wise affinity matrix by expanding the node distance matrix over image-token positions. A learnable per-head Linear(-D) is added to the attention logits as a residual bias, so farther nodes get lower attention. It replaces all self-attention layers of the Qwen2 backbone.

Global action reasoning: the action space is stop plus all observed but unvisited candidate nodes. The output format is <node>i</node> or <stop>. Non-adjacent targets are reached by shortest-path search, giving backtracking.

Training: single-step action prediction (SAP) with teacher-forced cross-entropy, on 80K R2R samples plus HM3D augmentation from ScaleVLN (500K samples for 0.5B, 200K for 7B). Stage 1 is 12.5K steps of mixed pretraining, stage 2 is 5K steps of R2R fine-tuning. Projector and LLM are fully fine-tuned, and the ViT is frozen.

setting.backbone: Qwen2 (0.5B and 7B, fully fine-tuned) + frozen SigLIP encoder + 2-layer MLP projector
setting.training_data: R2R train (14,093 trajectories, 80K SAP samples) + ScaleVLN HM3D augmentation (500K samples for 0.5B, 200K for 7B, 800 scenes)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (12 headings x 3 pitches, 60° FOV) per node, plus topological graph distances
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints: global action space of all observed unvisited candidates plus stop
setting.privileged: none (uses the simulator's discrete connectivity graph and node distances, as in standard R2R)

numbers_note: Table 1 prints most baseline numbers rounded to integers. The 7B row is the headline result. Ablations in Tables 2 and 3 use the 0.5B model on val unseen.
results: TagaVLM-7B reaches SR 51.09 / SPL 47.18 on R2R val-unseen, beating MapGPT (GPT-4V, zero-shot; SR 47.7 / SPL 38.1) by 3.39 SR and 9.08 SPL. The 0.5B model gets SR 45.72 and SPL 41.91. Both remain far below cross-modal methods such as ScaleVLN (SR 81). NaviLLM is not compared because it uses much more training data.
limitations: Only R2R in discrete environments is evaluated. There is no continuous-environment or real-robot test, which is left as future work.
Still far below specialist cross-modal transformers (e.g. ScaleVLN SR 81), and the comparison with zero-shot GPT-4V is fine-tuned vs zero-shot, so not like-for-like.
Compute limits meant the 7B model used only 200K augmented samples, and NaviLLM was excluded from comparison.
